readout_other: single-unit extracellular recording in the inferior colliculus with iontophoretic application of bicuculline and GABA
direction_notes: Bicuculline (a GABA-A antagonist) broadened echo duration tuning curves and decreased duration selectivity (nDW), while GABA application sharpened tuning curves and increased duration selectivity; effects were greater with shorter pulse duration and pulse-echo gap.

exposures.label: Pulse-echo pairs of tone/FM pulses presented to determine echo duration selectivity of IC neurons, with GABA/bicuculline iontophoresis

target.label: central nucleus of the bat inferior colliculus (IC)

timing.protocol_description: Initial characterisation used 4 ms tone pulses (0.5 ms rise-decay) delivered at 2 pulses/s via a loudspeaker 23 cm from the bat. Echo duration tuning was then studied with pulse-echo (P-E) pairs in which the pulse (P) was fixed at 1.5, 4.0 or 10 ms (mimicking terminal, approach and search phases of hunting) while the echo (E) duration was varied across eight values (1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20 ms); pulse and echo amplitudes were set 30 and 10 dB above each neuron's minimum threshold.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Ten E. fuscus (6 males, 4 females, 10–27 g, body weight, b.w.) were used for this study. As described in previous studies (Jen et al. 1987), the Xat head of a 1.8 cm nail was glued onto the exposed skull of each Nembutal anesthetized bat (45–59 mg/kg b.w.) with acrylic glue and dental cement 1 or 2 days before the recording session. Exposed tissue was treated with an antibiotic (Neosporin) to prevent inXammation. During recording, the bat was administered the neuroleptanalgesic, Innovar-Vet (Fentanyl 0.08 mg/kg b.w. Droperidol 4 mg/kg b.w.), and placed inside a bat holder (made of wire mesh) that was suspended in an elastic sling inside a double-wall sound-proof room (temperature $2 8 \mathrm { - } 3 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } )$ . The ceiling and inside walls of the room were covered with 3-in. convoluted polyurethane foam to reduce echoes. After Wxing the bat’s head with a set screw, small holes were made in the skull above the IC for insertion of 3 M KCl glass pipette electrodes (impedance: 5–10 M). Additional doses of Innovar-Vet were administered during later phases of recording when bats showed signs of discomfort. A local anesthetic (Lidocaine) was applied to the open wound area. The recording depth was read from the scale of a microdrive (David Kopf). A common indiVerent electrode (silver wire) was placed at the nearby temporal muscles. Each bat was used in one to Wve recording sessions on separate days and each recording session typically last for 2–6 h. The experiments were conducted according to NIH publication no. 85–23, “Principles of Laboratory Animal Care” and with the approval of the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of the University of Missouri-Columbia.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In this study, 98 IC neurons were isolated at depths between 119 and 1,898 -m. Their BFs and MTs ranged 20.3–73.9 kHz $( 3 6 . 5 \pm 7 . 4 \mathrm { { k H z } ) }$ and 18–55 dB SPL (42.5 § 7.1 dB SPL). The Wrst-spike latencies were between 9 and 22 ms $( 1 2 . 6 \pm 1 . 7 \mathrm { m s } )$ . Echo duration selectivity was studied for all 98 neurons. However, echo duration selectivity of only 54 neurons was studied during drug application because of loss of neurons throughout the course of study. Among them, 22 neurons received bicuculline application and 14 neurons received GABA application. The remaining 18 received bicuculline application Wrst. After recovery from the drug eVect, they then received GABA application. Therefore, echo duration selectivity was studied in 40 neurons during bicuculline application and in 32 neurons during GABA application.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Acoustic stimuli (4 ms with 0.5 ms rise–decay times, delivered at 2 pulses/s) were generated with an oscillator (KH model 1200) and a homemade electronic switch driven by a stimulator (Grass S88). These stimuli were then ampliWed after passing through a decade attenuator (HP 350D) before they were fed to a small condenser loudspeaker (AKG model CK 50, 1.5 cm diameter, 1.2 g) that was placed 23 cm away from the bat and 30° contralateral to the recording site. Calibration of the loudspeaker was performed with a ¼-in. microphone (B & K 4135) placed at the position of the bat’s head during recording using a measuring ampli-Wer (B & K 2607). The output of the loudspeaker was expressed in dB SPL in reference to 20 -Pa root mean square.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Each bat was used in one to Wve recording sessions on separate days
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: The echo duration selectivity of the IC neuron was studied by plotting its duration tuning curves using the number of impulses in response to eight durations (1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 20 ms) of single pulses

flags.reason: 20.3-73.9 kHz is the range of individual neurons' best frequencies (BF), used to set each neuron's own tone frequency; it is not a single fixed carrier frequency applied to every exposure.

the paper manipulates both a fixed 'pulse' duration (1.5, 4 or 10 ms) and a swept 'echo' duration (1-20 ms) as independent stimulus dimensions; which corresponds to pulse_duration_ms could not be resolved, so left not_reported and both are described in protocol_description.
paper states each bat was used in 'one to five recording sessions on separate days', a range rather than a single number.

provenance.notes: This study presents acoustic tone/FM pulses at ultrasonic-for-human frequencies (matched to each bat's hearing range) via a loudspeaker for auditory-neurophysiology characterisation of echolocation processing; it is not a focused/transcranial ultrasound neuromodulation study, so several exposure fields (pressure/intensity domains, a single fixed frequency) fit the schema only loosely.
